title: Probability of the special coordinate and disjointness
statement: Fix $n \ge 1$ and equip the sample space of the hard distribution with the uniform probability measure, so that a sample consists of a special coordinate $T \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, Alice's and Bob's bits $x_T, y_T$ at that coordinate, and an independent uniformly chosen label in $\{\text{neither},\text{leftOnly},\text{rightOnly}\}$ at each of the $n$ coordinates. For any fixed coordinate $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, the probability that the special coordinate satisfies $T = i$ and that the generated sets $X$ and $Y$ are disjoint equals \[ \frac{3}{4n}. \]
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number (so n ≥ 1)
i is a fixed coordinate in Fin n
measure is the uniform (volume) probability on the hard-distribution sample space
replaced: Under the hard distribution, $T=i$ and disjointness have probability $3/(4n)$.
